office_does: The coroner investigates sudden, unexpected and violent deaths in Okanogan County, determines cause and manner of death and works with families, law enforcement and medical providers.
race_blurb: Open seat: Coroner Dave Rodriguez is retiring. Chief Deputy Coroner Gene Davis, a former sheriff's detective sergeant, says the job is investigative; nurse practitioner Cindy Jensen (Prefers Independent Party) argues medical experience matters and pledges cost control in the office.

candidates.summary: Okanogan County chief deputy coroner since 2023 and a state-certified death investigator, after about 25 years at the sheriff's office as a K-9 handler, sergeant and detective sergeant.
highlights: Chief deputy coroner since 2023; investigated homicides and suspicious deaths at the sheriff's office [S1]
'You don't have to be a doctor, nurse or EMT. The primary thing is to be an investigator' [S3]
Promises 'a seamless transition within the Coroner's Office' [S1]

experience.basis: The retiring coroner's chief deputy with a long investigative career, running on continuity in the office.

candidates.summary: Nurse practitioner who owns a practice in Oroville and retired from the VA in 2025, running as an Independent with a medical rather than law-enforcement background.
highlights: Registered nurse since 1989 and nurse practitioner for 24 years; former VA home-based primary care provider [S1][S2]
'I am fiscally conservative'; says she has a plan to control the office's costs while maintaining services [S1]
Proposes more deputy coroners or volunteers to cut rural response times [S3]

experience.basis: No public-office or coroner record; runs as an outsider from health care ('I don't think you have to be a deputy to be a coroner').

spending.basis: Calls herself fiscally conservative and promises to control the office's costs, citing the county deficit; details unpublished.
